plan: SAT Math batch 3: Algebra 3, Advanced Math 4, Problem-Solving and Data Analysis 1, Geometry and Trigonometry 2; 3 student-produced responses; two hard items (coefficient matching with two cases, exponential factor per 2 years). Ideas that repeated ACT items 172 and 061 were dropped.

candidates.stem:
(ax + 3)(bx + 7) = 15x² + cx + 21
In the equation above, a, b and c are constants, the equation is true for all values of x, and a + b = 8. What is the greatest possible value of c ?
candidates.explanation: Expanding: abx² + (7a + 3b)x + 21. So ab = 15 and a + b = 8, giving {a, b} = {3, 5}. If a = 3, b = 5, then c = 21 + 15 = 36; if a = 5, b = 3, then c = 35 + 9 = 44. The greatest is 44.
hints: Expand the left side and match each coefficient.

strategy.explanation: Find a and b from ab = 15 and a + b = 8, then test both orders.

candidates.remember: Matching coefficients can leave more than one case; check them all.

author_checklist.hardness: Students must expand, set up ab = 15 with a + b = 8, and then notice that the two assignments of 3 and 5 give different values of c.

common_errors.rationale: 36 is the value of c when a = 3 and b = 5, the smaller of the two possibilities.
10 adds 3 and 7 without the coefficients a and b.

candidates.subskill: Equation of a circle with an unknown constant
candidates.stem: In the xy-plane, the graph of x² + y² + 8x − 6y = k is a circle with radius 6. What is the value of k ?
candidates.explanation: Complete the squares: (x + 4)² − 16 + (y − 3)² − 9 = k, so (x + 4)² + (y − 3)² = k + 25. The radius is 6, so k + 25 = 36 and k = 11.
hints: Complete the square for x and for y.

strategy.explanation: Write the equation in center-radius form.

candidates.remember: Completing the square adds constants to both sides.

common_errors.rationale: 36 is the square of the radius, before accounting for the completed squares.

candidates.subskill: Right-triangle trigonometry with a given ratio
candidates.stem: In right triangle ABC, angle C is the right angle, tan A = 5/12 and AB = 26. What is the length of BC ?
candidates.explanation: tan A = BC/AC = 5/12, so the sides are in the ratio 5 : 12 : 13. Since AB = 26 = 2 × 13, BC = 2 × 5 = 10.
hints: Which side is opposite angle A?
candidates.remember: A trig ratio gives a side ratio; scale it to the given side.

A.rationale: 5 uses the ratio without scaling by 2.

D.rationale: 24 is AC, the side adjacent to A.

candidates.stem: Which of the following values of x is a solution to the inequality 3 − 2x > 11 ?
candidates.explanation: 3 − 2x > 11 gives −2x > 8, so x < −4. Only −6 is less than −4.
hints: What happens to the inequality when you divide by a negative number?
candidates.remember: Dividing by a negative reverses the inequality.

B.rationale: −4 makes the two sides equal, so it is not a solution of the strict inequality.

D.rationale: 4 results from forgetting to reverse the inequality when dividing by −2.

candidates.subskill: System of linear inequalities in context
candidates.stem: Each week Maya runs r miles and bikes b miles. Running burns 110 calories per mile, and biking burns 40 calories per mile. She wants to burn at least 2,000 calories while covering no more than 30 miles in all. Which of the following choices of (r, b) meets both goals?
hints: Write one inequality for calories and one for distance.

strategy.explanation: Test each pair in both inequalities.

candidates.remember: A solution of a system must satisfy every inequality.

A.rationale: This covers 30 miles but burns only 1,900 calories.

D.rationale: This burns enough calories but covers 35 miles.

candidates.stem: The population of a town t years after 2020 is modeled by P(t) = 8,000(1.05)^(t/2). Which statement best describes how the population changes according to the model?
candidates.explanation: When t increases by 2, the exponent t/2 increases by 1, so P is multiplied by 1.05: a 5% increase every 2 years. (The yearly rate is √1.05 − 1 ≈ 2.47%, not exactly 2.5%.)
hints: What happens to the exponent when t increases by 2?
candidates.remember: In a(b)^(t/k), the factor b applies every k units of t.

author_checklist.hardness: Choices A and C are tempting shortcuts; students must see that the growth factor applies per 2 years and that halving a percent is not the same as taking a square root.

A.rationale: This ignores the division of t by 2 in the exponent.

B.rationale: This doubles the percent instead of the time period.

C.rationale: This halves the percent; compound growth makes the yearly rate about 2.47%, not 2.5%.

candidates.stem:
4/(x − 2) = 2/(x − 5)
What value of x satisfies the equation above?
candidates.explanation: Cross-multiply: 4(x − 5) = 2(x − 2), so 4x − 20 = 2x − 4, 2x = 16 and x = 8. Neither denominator is 0 at x = 8.
candidates.remember: Check that the solution doesn't make a denominator 0.

common_errors.rationale: −8 makes a sign error when collecting terms.

item.subskill: Solving a linear model for its input
item.stem: The total cost C, in dollars, to rent a kayak for h hours is given by C = 18 + 12h. A customer paid $78 to rent a kayak. For how many hours did the customer rent it?
item.remember: Remove the starting value before dividing by the rate.

D.rationale: 6 divides 78 by 12 and rounds, ignoring the $18 fee.

withdrawn.reason: withdrawn before review: same template as an app demo item (minimum of 3x² − 12x + 7); this item used 2x² − 12x + 7. Not resubmitted.

item.subskill: Vertex form that displays a minimum
item.stem:
f(x) = 2x² − 12x + 7
Which of the following equivalent forms of f(x) shows the minimum value of f as a constant or coefficient?
item.explanation: f(x) = 2(x² − 6x) + 7 = 2(x − 3)² − 18 + 7 = 2(x − 3)² − 11, which shows the minimum value −11.
hints: Factor 2 out of the x-terms first.

strategy.explanation: Check x = 0 in each choice: only A and D give 7, and only A also matches at x = 1.

item.remember: Vertex form a(x − h)² + k shows the minimum k when a > 0.

B.rationale: This completes the square with 6 instead of half of 6.

C.rationale: This has the wrong sign inside the square, which changes the function.

D.rationale: This is not equivalent; it expands to 4x² − 12x + 7.

item.subskill: Prediction from a line of best fit
item.stem: For a group of students, the line of best fit for test score y versus hours of practice x is y = 1.8x + 12. According to the line of best fit, what is the predicted test score for a student who practiced 15 hours?
item.remember: A line of best fit predicts by substitution.
